description: A team manager must decide whether to issue a formal performance warning to Nora after two missed client handoffs and must finalize a fair support plan for her ongoing client work.

shared_context.S1: Nora missed two client handoffs during the past month, and the delays were raised in the team's weekly review.
shared_context.S2: Elena decides whether the issue requires a formal performance warning and sets the resulting support plan.
shared_context.S3: The team handles several concurrent client escalations, and handoff expectations have not been written into a single shared checklist.
shared_context.S4: Elena's routine case-review protocol is a round-robin with two required speaking slots: Nora first gives one factual observation and any implementation requirement, then the HR business partner gives one factual observation and any implementation requirement. Elena waits until both people have clearly stated their input aloud; if a contribution is unclear or does not come through, the speaker repeats it before Elena summarizes and finalizes the response in the same meeting.

PF1.text: Nora observed three handoffs firsthand: in each case, the required client inputs were missing when Nora's work was due, Nora asked for the missing inputs in writing, and she completed the handoff within one business day after receiving them. Nora has also already agreed informally to serve as a peer feedback partner for four weeks if Elena formalizes that support.

PF2.text: Marcus confirmed this week that Nora's approved work accommodation limits her to exactly three concurrent client escalations and requires written agendas and prompts at least two business days before performance-review discussions. Nora asked HR to discuss the implementation details in the case review rather than circulate the medical basis.

acceptance_conditions: The response must not issue Nora a formal performance warning because the observed delays resulted from missing inputs rather than failure to complete work after inputs arrived.
The record must identify the handoff process and missing inputs as the documented root cause.
The record must classify the root cause as a handoff process problem rather than an individual performance failure.
The record must state that exactly three handoffs were observed firsthand.
Nora's active client-escalation load must be capped at exactly three.
Performance-review agendas and prompts must be provided at least two business days in advance.
Nora must be assigned a peer feedback partner for four weeks.

content_checks.C2: ('missing client inputs' in decisions['documented_root_cause']) or ('missing upstream client inputs' in decisions['documented_root_cause']) or ('input dependencies' in decisions['documented_root_cause'])
content_checks.C5: any(c['type'] == 'support_plan' and c['target'] == 'Nora' and (('peer feedback' in c['detail']) or ('peer-feedback' in c['detail'])) and (('four weeks' in c['detail']) or ('4 weeks' in c['detail']) or ('four-week' in c['detail'])) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: decisions['formal_warning_issued'] == False and decisions['root_cause_category'] == 'process_gap' and decisions['handoff_count'] == 3

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The three firsthand handoffs change the record to exactly 3 and classify the cause as a process gap driven by missing inputs rather than an individual warning, while Nora's prior agreement changes the support plan to a peer feedback partnership lasting exactly four weeks.

The approved accommodation changes Nora's workload cap to exactly three concurrent client escalations and changes review preparation to written agendas and prompts exactly two business days in advance.
